segment: SHOWHAUS arrange mode (2026-11-17): (a) renters and buyers who just secured, or are about to secure, a home and want to know whether their furniture fits before move-in; (b) vendors, landlords and agents with a listing who could give buyers an arrange-it-yourself plan. Two outside the assumed segment.
grounding: Phrasing lifted from r/AusRenting, r/sydney, r/AusFinance, r/AusPropertyChat and r/interiordecorating threads on moving in ("will my couch fit through the door", "measured the room with a tape and drew it on graph paper", "the listing photos use a wide-angle lens so you can't tell size", "floor plan isn't to scale", "used IKEA planner but it only does one room", "Roomle/Planner 5D wanted me to sign up"), agent forum posts on floor plans ("buyers ask for the floor plan more than anything", "virtual staging gets complaints if it's too fake"), and the 2026-11-17 gate panel ("a render, not a real place"; "the plan gives real sizes").

personas.who: Mia, 27, physio, signed a lease on a 1-bed in Marrickville yesterday
attrs: owns a 3-seat sofa (2.3 m), a queen bed, a 1.6 m desk
patience low on phone, high on laptop at night
won't sign up for anything to try it
only has the listing photos and the floor plan JPG from the agent
anxious the sofa won't fit the living nook
personas.last_time: Last move she measured with her phone's AR ruler at the inspection, got it wrong by 20 cm and the sofa blocked the balcony door.

personas.who: Tom and Jess, 31 and 30, about to exchange on a 2-bed unit in Ryde
attrs: deciding whether their 6-seat dining table works or they sell it
share everything with each other over WhatsApp
personas.last_time: Drew the unit on graph paper from the floor plan and cut paper squares for each piece of furniture; argued about which wall the TV goes on.

personas.who: Daniel, 38, IT contractor, just got approved for a 3-bed townhouse rental in Kellyville
attrs: kids 6 and 9, needs a desk spot for working from home
has used IKEA Planner and Planner 5D
patient if the tool is precise
wants exact cm and door swings
personas.last_time: Gave up on Planner 5D after it wanted an account and the free tier hid the dimension tool.

personas.who: Lorraine, 66, retiree, downsizing from a house in Baulkham Hills to a 2-bed villa
attrs: uses Facebook and email on an iPad
must decide which furniture to keep before the move
has the villa brochure with a floor plan
personas.last_time: Asked her daughter to measure the villa rooms on the second inspection and wrote the sizes on the back of the brochure.

personas.who: Arjun, 24, grad engineer, about to sign for a share-house room in Parramatta
attrs: one bedroom 3.0 × 3.2 m, no plan, only photos
owns a double bed, a desk, a clothes rack
everything through TikTok and group chats
sceptic: 'it's one room, I'll just measure'
personas.last_time: Bought a desk on Marketplace that didn't fit next to the bed and had to resell it.

personas.who: Grace, 35, nurse, shortlisted 3 rentals in Penrith, inspecting Saturday
attrs: comparing which home fits her furniture best
uses the SHOWHAUS-style shortlist idea already in Notes
personas.last_time: Took the wrong unit last year because the second bedroom looked bigger in photos than it was.

personas.who: Michelle, 44, sales agent at an independent agency in the Inner West
attrs: buyers ask for the floor plan more than anything
pays for floor plans and photos per listing
has tried virtual staging and had complaints it looked fake
would pay if it wins listings
personas.last_time: A buyer walked from a sale because the second bedroom couldn't fit a queen bed — found out at the second inspection.

personas.who: Steve, 52, private landlord with 2 units in Liverpool, re-letting one next month
attrs: lists through a cheap online agent
sceptic of anything that costs money
no floor plan, only a tape measure
doesn't want his address shown more than necessary
personas.last_time: Showed the unit to 11 groups; half said at the door the bedroom was too small for their bed.

personas.who: Priya, 39, vendor selling her 2-bed apartment in Chatswood herself (with a low-fee agent)
attrs: has the strata floor plan PDF
wants the listing to stand out
would pay up to $100 for something that helps it sell
compares everything to REA's premiere listing
personas.last_time: Paid for photo touch-ups that made the rooms look bigger; buyers complained at inspection.

personas.who: Ben, 33, property manager, 180 doors in the Hills district
attrs: happy with REA + his PM software
would never pay out of pocket; landlord pays
worries about anything that creates tenant disputes
uses floor plans from the photographer
personas.last_time: A tenant broke a lease after 2 weeks because their furniture didn't fit; he had to re-let it.

personas.who: Hannah, 29, interior design student at TAFE
personas.last_time: Built a client's living room in SketchUp from a photo of a hand-drawn plan; took two evenings.

personas.who: Raj, 47, removalist business owner in Blacktown
attrs: quotes jobs by volume and access
would love customers to show what goes where
pays for tools that save a site visit
sceptic of apps customers won't use
personas.last_time: Spent 40 minutes on a job carrying a sofa that didn't fit up the stairs and had to take it back.
